properties.name: reflow2 can accurately say where it is, which means knowing what it has already DONE — because on a shared design the cost of not knowing is two people building the same thing twice
properties.statement:
Anthony, 2026-08-23, in two statements. The first is the requirement:

> *"reflow2 needs to be able to accurately show where it is (and that means knowing what it's done)."*

The second is why it is not a tidiness concern, and it raised the priority:

> *"if multiple people are working on a project from different machines and if reflow2 is not able to accurately mark progress, one user may finish a task (or make some progress) and another user may repeat completing that same thing - only to find out that it was completed already. now you have 2 solutions developed from 2 different users. that's a pretty big deal to me."*

⭐ **THE ESCALATION IS THE POINT.** For one person, a stale graph costs time and the user catches it. For two people on two machines it costs a **DIVERGENT IMPLEMENTATION** — and that is not a graph merge, it is two working solutions to one problem that somebody now has to choose between and throw one away. reflow2's own three-way merge driver reconciles the DESIGN RECORD; nothing reconciles two independently written implementations, and nothing should have to.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📐 WHAT IS ALREADY COVERED, MEASURED 2026-08-23 rather than assumed

✅ **COLLISION WHILE WORKING.** `claim_region` / `claim_report` / `cap:cluster-claims`, and `parallel-work`'s isolated worktree. Advisory by design — a claim never blocks a write — but it answers "is someone in here right now?".

✅ **PLANNED WORK, DELIVERED.** `arrival_delta` returns `delivered` / `deferred` / `discontinued` / `outstanding`, and **`delivered` is DERIVED FROM THE GOLDEN THREAD, never stored** — deliberately, so there is no second source of truth able to disagree. Verified on `epoch:instruments-stop-overstating`: five scheduled items, five `delivered`, `missed_obligations: []`, `ready_to_cut: true`. **This half works, and it is the model for the rest.**

✅ **THE SHARED RECORD MOVING.** `sync_status` reports `behind` and names the nodes a graph has not seen, so a machine can learn the record moved under it.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 WHAT IS NOT COVERED, AND IT IS EXACTLY HIS SCENARIO

❌ **AN OBSERVED FINDING BEING RETIRED.** 274 TemporalFacts, all `basis: measured`, **7 carrying a `valid_to`** — 2.6%. 200 of the 267 open ones describe a node that has since been CHANGED. A finding that motivated a fix survives the fix. User B reads it, believes it, and redoes the work.

❌ **THE THREE "WHO" AXES SAY EVERYTHING EXCEPT DONE.** `AUTHORED_BY` = who wrote it. `CLAIMS` = who is in it right now. `OWNED_BY` = whose ground it is. **None says it is finished**, and "finished" is derivable only for work that was PLANNED into an increment.

❌ **CROSS-MACHINE CLAIM LIVENESS IS `unknown` BY CONSTRUCTION.** A claim made on another machine cannot be checked against a live process, so it reads `unknown` — never `free`, which is the honest choice, and also not an answer to "did they finish?".

⇒ **THE ASYMMETRY IS THE REQUIREMENT.** reflow2 can say what was PLANNED and delivered because delivery is COMPUTED. It cannot say what was OBSERVED and superseded, because an observation is ASSERTED once and nothing ever revisits it. A measurement cannot be derived the way delivery can — nobody can compute whether a timing taken on 2026-08-21 is still true — so the mechanism must differ even though the need is identical.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📌 WHAT THIS REQUIRES, stated as a property rather than as a design

That a reader — a person or an agent, on any machine — can tell **what this design has already achieved** from the design itself, without asking someone. Specifically: that a finding which has been acted on is distinguishable from one that has not, and that the distinction survives being carried between machines through the committed export.

⚠️ **HOW is deliberately not settled here.** `dec:idea-how-does-the-graph-learn-what-a-session-invalidated` holds six options with their costs, and this requirement does not choose among them. Two half-measures already exist and neither is sufficient alone: `capture-session`'s test 7 (added 2026-08-23) catches the case where the session that invalidates a finding also closes it, and misses the far commoner case where a different session, days later, does the invalidating; a detector would reach that case and cannot know whether a candidate is genuinely stale.

⚠️ **BOUND: the multi-user cost is REASONED, not observed.** Anthony describes it as a risk he cares about, and the single-user version of it happened twice on 2026-08-23 — once in the session that recorded this, once on his other machine. **Nobody has yet watched two people build the same thing twice on this design.** The reasoning is that a mechanism which fails for one reader fails worse for two, and that is an argument, not a measurement.
